concession.modelName: Build-Own-Operate-Transfer with defined cost-recovery + return cap
concession.operator: Noida Toll Bridge Company Ltd (NTBCL, IL&FS group)
concession.grantingAuthority: New Okhla Industrial Development Authority (NOIDA), Govt of Uttar Pradesh
concession.tollEndCondition: Tolls were to end once the concessionaire recovered project cost plus a 20% return on paid-up share capital - a rare toll road with an explicit recovery formula

extensions.description: Concession agreement amended to include 'link road/approach' costs and other additions into recoverable project cost, pushing the recovery end-point further away

projectCost.note: ~Rs 308 crore initial project cost; the 'recoverable cost' was later expanded through amendments to several times this figure

funding.label: NTBCL equity (IL&FS-led; NOIDA took equity stake in lieu of land/cash contribution)
NOIDA land grant along the corridor (developed and sold as real estate)

amount.note: Real-estate income was substantial but its offset against recoverable cost is disputed

revenue.note: ~Rs 120 crore annual toll revenue reported around the time of litigation

annualRevenue.note: Car one-way toll ~Rs 55-65. NTBCL is listed so quarterly revenues are available via stock-exchange filings.

timeline.title: Concession agreement signed with NOIDA
timeline.description: BOT concession with an explicit exit: tolls end after recovering project cost plus 20% return on paid-up capital.

timeline.title: Flyway opens
timeline.description: The 9.2 km Delhi-Noida bridge and approaches open as India's first major urban BOT toll road.

timeline.title: Recoverable-cost definition expanded
timeline.description: Amendments fold additional costs into the recoverable base even as cumulative collections far exceed the original Rs 308 crore outlay.

timeline.title: Allahabad High Court orders toll-free DND
timeline.description: HC holds that NOIDA residents cannot be tolled and questions continued collection beyond cost recovery; Supreme Court proceedings follow and tolls continue during litigation.

timeline.title: Tolling continues amid litigation
timeline.description: Matter remains contested between NOIDA, NTBCL and petitioner groups; tolls continue while 'recoverable cost' accounting stays opaque.

analysis.summary: DND is the clearest Indian example of a toll road that should have stopped charging by its own contract: it has an explicit cost-plus-20%-return formula, yet tolls continue because the definition of recoverable cost kept growing and litigation replaced enforcement.
reasonsStillTolled: Contract amendments repeatedly enlarged what counts as 'project cost' eligible for recovery
Real-estate income from NOIDA-granted land is not clearly netted against recoverable cost
Litigation (Allahabad HC 2016 order, SC appeals) left the status quo - tolling - in place
NTBCL's listed status gives it standing and resources to defend continuation
openQuestions: What is NTBCL's current claimed unrecovered balance under the concession?
How much has been collected cumulatively since 2001 vs the original and amended cost bases?
What real-estate revenue has NTBCL earned from corridor land, and why isn't it offset against tolls?
What is the current legal status of the Allahabad HC toll-free order?
